question: Compare the historical CLOUD definition with the available modern cloud definition. Does the historical entry establish whether electricity causes cloud formation? In at most 160 words cite exact returned historical and Wikipedia source IDs. Preserve uncertainty and label paraphrases. Omit personal names unless their exact spelling is established by the returned text.

result.answer:
Historical: "CLOUD, a collection of vapours suspended in the atmosphere" (bri-0059-891965a7ca3e). It adds that clouds form from aqueous vapours, once invisible, closely united with the atmosphere [bri-0059-891965a7ca3e:region-11:0]. It names electricity as an agent in cloud formation by some authorities, but concludes this remains "a question" not "ascertained," with "little or no foundation" for a theory [bri-0059-891965a7ca3e:region-15:0]. So the entry does not establish that electricity causes cloud formation; it treats the link as unresolved, while stating it is certain clouds contain the electric fluid [bri-0059-891965a7ca3e].

Modern: Wikipedia defines a cloud as "a visible mass of condensed droplets or frozen crystals suspended in the atmosphere" (wiki-593754-1320064819-5941026ced18). Paraphrase: the historical definition is simpler and says vapours; the modern definition specifies condensed droplets or frozen crystals and adds visibility.

A Cluster diagram or clustering diagram is a general type of diagram, which represents some kind of cluster. A cluster in general is a group or bunch of several discrete items that are close to each other.

The cluster diagram figures a cluster, such as a network diagram figures a network, a flow diagram a process or movement of objects, and a tree diagram an abstract tree. But all these diagrams can be considered interconnected: A network diagram can be seen as a special orderly arranged kind of cluster diagram. A cluster diagram is a mesh kind of network diagram. A flow diagram can be seen as a line type of network diagram, and a tree diagram a tree type of network diagram.

In architecture a comparison diagram is sometimes called a cluster diagram.

In astronomy diagrams of star clusters, galaxy clusters or globular clusters.

In brainstorming a cluster diagrams is also called cloud diagram. They can be considered "are a type of non-linear graphic organizer that can help to systematize the generation of ideas based upon a central topic.
